walkthroughs.body_html:
Individual Oral — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Individual Oral brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Individual Oral.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term unreliable narrator in 1961?
options: Wayne Booth
Northrop Frye
F R Leavis
Mikhail Bakhtin

mcqs.q: Which Marquez novel exemplifies magic realism?
options: Love in the Time of Cholera
One Hundred Years of Solitude
The Autumn of the Patriarch
Chronicle of a Death Foretold

mcqs.q: What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Gothic just means scary stories with vampires and ghosts.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.

mcqs.q: What did Romantic poets value in nature?
options: Nature as a source of spiritual insight and emotional truth, accessed through imagination — not picturesque scenery for its own sake.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
Romantic poets just liked to write about pretty landscapes.
